turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Grace Oileron, and this must be the patient. Nice shin guards, buddy.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Game today. Right after this, so he's in a hurry, I'm his dad Javier.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Nice to meet you. Can you confirm his full name and date of birth for me?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Mateo Herrera, April 21st, 2017. He's nine.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thanks, so what are we looking at today? Warts, he's got a couple on his right pointer finger,

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: one on his left thumb, and one on his knee. The finger ones started maybe five months ago, and they keep multiplying.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have you tried anything for them?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: The drugstore salicylic acid, the 17 % liquid, every night for about six weeks, didn't really do much. That's pretty common.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: It can take months.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Do they hurt him? No, not really. He picks at them, though, and bites his nails.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have they bled or gotten infected?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Is he generally healthy? Any problems with his immune system or a lot of infections?

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: No, he's healthy. No medicines, no allergies. Oh, and his sister Lucia has one on the bottom of her foot, if that matters.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: She's not here today. Good to know they do spread in families. Okay Mateo, let me see your hands. On the right index finger, there are two rough, skin -colored bumps, 5mm and 3mm, with tiny black dots in them.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: On the left thumb,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: there's a 6mm one right next to the nail fold. And on the right knee, a 4mm one. These are all common warts, no redness or signs of infection around them.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Can you also look at his arms? He has these little rough bumps on the backs of his upper arms, like sandpaper.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Sure,

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: yes,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: on the backs of both upper arms. There are lots of tiny, pinpoint, rough bumps around the hair follicles. Skin colored to pink, that's keratosis pilaris. It's really common, it's harmless, and it often gets better as kids get older.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Oh good, is there anything for it?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: A urea 10 % cream once a day after the bath helps smooth it out. It's over the counter. Use a gentle soap, and don't scrub hard. Now for the warts. I'd like to freeze them today with liquid nitrogen. It stings for a few seconds. Is that okay,

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Mateo? He's nodding. Go for it. All right.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm doing all four warts. Two freestyle cycles each. Here comes the cold.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Great job.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: You didn't even flinch.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: What should we expect now? They may get red,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: form a blister, or turn dark over the next few days. That's normal. Children's acetaminophen per the package directions, if they are sore. Once the blisters heal, in about a week, restart the salicylic acid at night. Soak first, file the dead skin with an emery board that only he uses, then cover duct

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: tape. Duct tape, really?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Really, it helps keep the medicine on, and try to keep him from picking and biting. That's how they spread. If one gets very red,

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: swollen,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: or his pus, give us a call.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Got it. Does he need to stay home from school?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: No, he can go to school and play sports.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Where does he go? Maple Grove Elementary, 4th grade. Nice.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Warts usually take two to four freezing sessions, so let's bring him back in three to four weeks for another round.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: What's the best number for you?" Mycel 555 -0191.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Perfect.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Good luck at the game, Mateo. Thanks,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Dr.

turns.speaker: caregiver
turns.text: Oyelaren. Say thank you, Mateo. Okay, he said it.
